PPL Corporation (NYSE: PPL) is a $9 billion S&P 500 regulated electric utility serving 3.5 million customers across Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Virginia, and Rhode Island. Its internship and co-op program spans six functional tracks (Engineering, IT, Accounting/Finance, Business, HR, Skilled Crafts) with pay averaging $23–$28 per hour, subsidized housing in Pennsylvania, housing stipends in Kentucky, and a year-round recruiting cycle. Pennsylvania's summer 2027 postings open as early as August 2026.

## What Is a PPL Corporation Internship?


The PPL Corporation internship is a paid program where students work on real utility infrastructure projects across two separate subsidiaries: PPL Electric Utilities in Pennsylvania (summer only) and LG&E/KU Energy in Kentucky (year-round, three semesters). PPL holds a 3.5/5 rating on Indeed with 335 reviews, while the LG&E/KU subsidiary scores a notably higher 4.0/5 on Glassdoor with 341 reviews. All positions include assigned mentors, professional development events, and a pathway to permanent employment.


## When Do PPL Corporation Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


PPL operates on staggered recruiting timelines across its two subsidiaries. Pennsylvania posts summer internships in August through September, earlier than most large companies. Kentucky runs three cycles per year (summer, fall, spring) with rolling postings. Students can target both subsidiaries if they apply at the right time.

*How to read this page: our dates come from tracking previous recruiting cycles and daily posting data. Treat them as informed estimates based on historical patterns, not confirmed dates. The company's official careers page is always the most current source. If a role is posted there, go by that, even if this page suggests the window hasn't opened yet.*


### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


PPL's Pennsylvania subsidiary opens its application window in August through September, weeks earlier than most S&P 500 companies. With rolling review, the earliest applicants face the least competition and the widest selection of tracks. Kentucky's separate January through February window adds a second chance, but summer slots in engineering and finance fill quickly. PPL's official internship page states ongoing review within each cycle window, confirming that delays directly reduce your options.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


PPL publishes specific eligibility requirements for its corporate and craft worker programs, including GPA minimums.


• **Enrollment:** Full-time student (minimum 12 semester hours) at an accredited four-year college or university


• **GPA (corporate tracks):** 3.0 minimum required


• **GPA (craft worker):** 2.5 minimum required (enrolled in a technical program, not a four-year degree)


• **Age:** Must be 18 years or older


• **Work authorization:** US work authorization required; no mention of visa sponsorship


• **Transcript:** Official student transcript submission required with application


• **Drug testing:** Mandatory pre-employment drug test for ALL positions


### Does PPL Have a GPA Cutoff for Interns?


Yes. PPL explicitly requires a minimum 3.0 GPA for corporate internship and co-op positions across engineering, IT, finance, business, and HR tracks. The Kentucky craft-worker and engineering tracks have a lower threshold of 2.5 GPA. There is no published upper target. PPL also requires an official student transcript submission, so your GPA is verified as part of the application, not self-reported.

## What Is the PPL Corporation Application and Interview Process Like?


PPL uses a straightforward application process through two separate portals depending on your target location.


1. **Choose your subsidiary and cycle.** PPL Electric Utilities (Pennsylvania) is summer only with postings August through September. LG&E/KU Energy (Kentucky) is year-round with summer postings January through February. If eligible, apply to both on their respective timelines.


2. **Search and apply online.** PPL uses iCIMS (careers-pplweb.icims.com) for Pennsylvania; LG&E/KU uses their own portal (lge-ku.com/careers). Filter by Internships & Co-ops. Upload resume and official transcript.


3. **Application review (rolling).** Hiring teams review applications on a rolling basis within each cycle window. Early applicants get priority.


4. **Interview.** Glassdoor rates PPL interview difficulty at 2.9/5 with 73% positive experience. Expect behavioral and technical components depending on your track.


5. **Pre-employment drug testing.** Mandatory for ALL PPL positions. Background check is also standard.


6. **Offer and onboarding.** PA offers typically extend November through December for summer start. Full-day HR orientation, mentor assignment, and professional development kick off the program.


For application assistance, contact PPL Corporate Recruiting at HRCorporateRecruiting@pplweb.com or (610) 774-7777 option 4.

## How Do You Stand Out at PPL Corporation?


First, apply to BOTH Pennsylvania and Kentucky on their respective timelines. PPL runs two completely separate programs with staggered windows. Most applicants target only one, so applying to both doubles your chances. Be explicit about why you want to work in each region's specific grid challenges. Second, build a grid-relevant project before you apply. PPL invests $4.4 billion annually in infrastructure modernization. A power flow analysis in MATLAB/Python (Engineering), a rate case financial model (Finance), or a grid reliability data visualization (IT) gives you a behavioral answer most candidates lack. Third, demonstrate that you understand the regulated utility business model. PPL operates under state public utility commission regulation, meaning its revenue and capital plans are set through regulatory proceedings. Reference rate cases, the generation-vs-distribution distinction, and PPL's $170 million in cumulative O&M savings through automation.

## FAQ


### When should I apply for the PPL summer 2027 internship?


It depends on location. For Pennsylvania (PPL Electric Utilities), apply in September to October 2026 when postings go live in August to September. For Kentucky (LG&E/KU), apply in January to February 2027. Pennsylvania's timeline is earlier than most companies, so prepare now.


### Does PPL have rolling admissions or a hard deadline?


Rolling. PPL reviews applications on an ongoing basis within each cycle window. Kentucky posts for all three semesters (summer, fall, spring) with rolling review. Pennsylvania's window is narrower (August through December) but still rolling. Apply early for the best track selection.


### What GPA does PPL require for interns?


PPL requires a minimum 3.0 GPA for corporate internship and co-op positions. Kentucky craft-worker internships have a lower threshold of 2.5 GPA. An official student transcript submission is required with your application, so your GPA is verified, not self-reported.


### What is the PPL internship interview process like?


PPL's interview is rated 2.9 out of 5 difficulty on Glassdoor, and 73% of candidates report a positive experience. Expect behavioral and technical questions depending on your track. All positions require pre-employment drug testing, which is mandatory company-wide.


### Does PPL offer return offers to interns?


PPL does not publish a conversion rate, but its official internship page states many roles lead to permanent employment. The utility industry generally has high intern conversion rates, and PPL's $4.4 billion annual infrastructure investment suggests growing workforce needs across all functions.


### How much does the PPL internship pay?


A confirmed Spring 2027 Science Intern posting lists $23 to $28 per hour. Indeed reports an average of $23.26 per hour across all PPL intern types, 15% above the national average. Pennsylvania interns also receive subsidized housing; Kentucky offers housing stipends or course fee reimbursement.


### What skills does PPL look for in interns?


PPL emphasizes power systems knowledge, analytical ability, safety awareness, and discipline-specific technical skills. Engineering interns need power analysis or CAD experience. Finance interns need Excel and accounting fundamentals. A grid-relevant project differentiates your application from generic submissions.


### Can I apply to both PPL Pennsylvania and Kentucky programs?


Yes. The two subsidiaries (PPL Electric Utilities in Pennsylvania and LG&E/KU in Kentucky) run completely separate programs with different ATS portals, timelines, and hiring teams. Applying to both on their respective schedules doubles your chances without any conflict.
